answer: A place with genuinely interesting architecture that comes to mind is Ahsan Manzil, an old palace in Old Dhaka, right on the bank of the Buriganga river. It was built in the nineteenth century as the residence of the Nawabs of Dhaka, and today it is a museum, which I visited while staying with my sister last year. People often call it the Pink Palace because of its colour, and it is a striking example of the Indo-Saracenic style, which mixes European and Mughal influences. What fascinated me was the [[craftsmanship]]; the arches, pillars and balconies are full of detail, and a grand staircase at the front leads up to the large dome at the centre of the building. The building is [[ornate]] without feeling excessive, and it blends beauty with clever practical design, such as high ceilings and wide verandas that keep the rooms cool in the heat. I found it remarkable how [[sophisticated]] the design was, considering it was built long before air conditioning. Inside, the rooms display furniture, portraits and household objects from the period, which give you a sense of how the family lived. Standing inside, I felt a real sense of admiration for the skill of the people who created it. Honestly, modern buildings, for all their convenience, rarely have this kind of soul. I think architecture like this tells us a great deal about the culture and values of the past, which is exactly what makes it so [[compelling]] to me. It also reminds me how important it is to [[conserve]] such buildings in a city that is changing so fast.

followUps.q: Do you prefer old or modern buildings?
followUps.answer: For beauty and character, I definitely prefer old buildings. Modern buildings are more comfortable and practical, of course, but they often look the same, whereas old buildings tell you something about the place and its history.

followUps.q: Was it crowded when you visited?
followUps.answer: Yes, fairly crowded, as it is one of the most popular sights in Old Dhaka. There were school groups and families everywhere, but it was still possible to find quieter corners to look around.

note: Unnamed palace 'built centuries ago' made Ahsan Manzil (19th century, Nawabs of Dhaka, Buriganga) with accurate features (dome, staircase, verandas); added the museum interior and conservation; added mark 'conserve'.
